issues.description: Duplicate 'transcriber_error' entry in the error-type tuple signals an unaudited hand-typed list.
issues.detail: All three reviewers flagged that 'transcriber_error' appears twice in the 14-element tuple. Semantically harmless for membership testing, but it advertises that the list was assembled without audit. Deduplicate and lift to a module-level frozenset (or dict keyed by type) so the catalog becomes inspectable, testable, and duplicate-resistant.

issues.description: logger.error calls dropped from the error path, weakening observability.
issues.detail: The old code logged each error type at error/warning level before pushing the frame. The consolidated branch only calls push_error, which does not reliably surface to logs. Production debugging is now harder for every error class. Restore a logger.error inside the consolidated branch, or document that push_error logs.

issues.description: Fourteen distinct error types collapsed into one undifferentiated 'Error:' frame, losing semantic distinctions.
issues.detail: Auth, quota, rate limiting, throttling, session limits, and 'insufficient_audio_activity' are different facts with different retry semantics (terminal vs retryable vs informational). The new code emits 'Error: <error>' for all of them, stripping the message_type prefix. Downstream consumers and humans reading logs cannot discriminate. Include message_type in the pushed error and consider a category/severity table.

issues.description: Inner try/except in _receive_messages still swallows all exceptions, potentially defeating the loop fix.
issues.detail: The PR's stated goal is to let websocket disconnects propagate to the outer reconnect loop. But the per-message 'except Exception' inside the async-for catches everything, including disconnects raised mid-iteration on some websocket libraries. Narrow to (json.JSONDecodeError, KeyError, ValueError) so the disconnect path is actually reachable.

issues.description: No regression test demonstrating the infinite-loop bug or proving the fix.
issues.detail: The headline claim is an infinite loop on websocket disconnect blocking the entire process. Without a test that hangs on the old code and passes on the new, this fix can silently regress when someone re-adds defensive try/except around _process_messages. Add a failing-then-passing test that exercises the disconnect path.

changelog/3233.fixed.md ends without a newline. Cosmetic, but POSIX convention and most lint configs expect a trailing newline, and existing changelog entries presumably have one. One-character fix to match repository style.

synthesis.summary: The panel agrees the core loop fix — removing the swallow-and-log wrapper so websocket disconnects propagate to the reconnect loop — is directionally correct, but the error-handling consolidation that ships alongside it is sloppy. 'transcriber_error' appears twice in the new tuple, per-type logger.error calls were dropped, and fourteen distinct error semantics collapse into one generic 'Error:' frame. The inner try/except still catches Exception broadly, which may defeat the very disconnect-propagation the PR is trying to enable. No regression test demonstrates the infinite-loop bug or proves it fixed. Verdict: needs work before landing — lift the error catalog to data, restore logging and message_type prefix, tighten the inner except, and add a disconnect regression test.
